methods.name: workdown.export
methods.summary: Export a Jira issue as the Workdown document an Exchange would share
methods.description: Read-only. Reads one issue as the caller, checks it against the named profile, and returns its Workdown document. Never stores or publishes anything. The document contains only the profile's allowlisted fields; nothing else on the issue is ever included. An optional field that is empty or not configured is omitted. Start date is found by its stable semantic identity, never by display name or a fixed field ID, so equivalent issues on different sites produce the same document. The caller must be able to read the issue. An issue that does not exist and one the caller cannot read produce the same forbidden error. An issue the caller can read but that the profile forbids sharing, such as one with issue-level security, produces issue-ineligible; it is returned only to a caller who can already read the issue and never discloses restricted content. If eligibility cannot be determined, the export fails with eligibility-undetermined; uncertainty is never permission. App-level access never authorizes disclosure. An issue that does not satisfy the profile produces profile-mismatch. A field that cannot be resolved to exactly one supported field produces field-unresolved. A field or value that cannot be read produces field-unreadable. The document includes a summary of each eligible direct child of the Epic, read through Jira's system parent relationship as the caller. Completed children are included. Grandchildren, subtasks of children, linked issues and the legacy Epic Link are never included. Children are ordered by immutable issue ID in lexical order, so the same content produces the same bytes regardless of how Jira ordered or paged its results. A child summary contains only identity, title, link, type, status and resolution; it has no description, comments or modification time. Children the caller cannot read, and children with issue-level security, are omitted silently, as Jira itself omits them from the caller's results: the document, errors and logs reveal no identity, title, count or reason for them. An Epic with no eligible children produces a document without a Children section. The export reads every page of children. If the listing cannot be read completely, the export fails with children-unreadable; a smaller snapshot is never returned and no child count is invented. A failed export never returns a partial document. Provisional application limits are 262144 UTF-8 bytes for the complete canonical document and 100 eligible direct children. Equality is allowed. Exceeding these limits produces Document too large (-32008) or Too many children (-32009), respectively; neither error is retryable without a source-content change. Excluded children do not count toward the child limit. Limit failures include no document, source values, counts, or diagnostics. Identical content on retry produces identical canonical bytes for direct comparison. Invalid required values fail the whole candidate with a sanitized error.
